question: Elena knitted 63 blanket squares in each of 9 weeks. She had to unravel 18 of them because the colours clashed badly. Her friend Piotr, who knits more slowly than Elena, contributed 77 squares to the same blanket. Every square in the finished blanket took 5 metres of wool. The charity shop that will sell it opens at half past eight and has 240 members on its mailing list. How many metres of wool went into the blanket?

Farah counted 200 beads in her tin and then found 7 more under the table. Each bead is worth 5 cents at the craft shop, so she worked out the value of the whole tin in cents rather than dollars. She divided that value equally between 3 charity jars. Her brother Idris, who had saved less than she had, added 69 cents to the jar Farah had filled first. Farah has been beading since she was a dozen years old. How many cents are in that jar now?

A builder had 57 boxes of floor tiles in his van and picked up 13 more from the yard. Every box holds 4 tiles. A neighbour gave him 72 loose tiles left over from her kitchen, and the merchant threw in 51 more as a goodwill gesture. Laying the hallway and the bathroom used up 327 tiles. The van is 6 metres long, and the builder quotes his jobs in days rather than in hours. How many tiles does the builder have left?

A conference centre had 170 stacking chairs and borrowed 16 more from the church hall. The chairs were shared out equally between 6 meeting rooms. From the Oak room 24 chairs were then taken away for a talk in the garden. The centre later set out 4 side rooms so that each one matched the Oak room exactly, chair for chair. The car park outside holds 95 vehicles. How many chairs were set out in those 4 side rooms altogether?

A garden centre started the morning with 174 crates of bedding plants and sent 162 crates off to a landscaping job. Each crate still on site holds 6 pots. A local school returned 61 pots it had not planted after all. A supplier then delivered 76 more pots to the same bench. The centre's price labels are printed in pence rather than pounds. How many pots are on the bench now?

A hotel laundry started the day with 228 towels on the rack. Housekeeping took 78 of them upstairs to the guest rooms. A delivery from the supplier then added 72 fresh towels to the same rack. Every towel now on that rack is cut into 4 cleaning cloths. Each cloth is finished with 6 stitched loops around its edge. How many stitched loops will the whole rack need?

A campsite had 36 tent pegs in the store hut. The warden bought 68 more from the outdoor shop, and a departing group left 50 behind. Each peg is wrapped in 5 turns of tape before it goes into a kit bag. Every turn of tape uses 6 centimetres from the roll. The campsite has 24 pitches beside the river. How many centimetres of tape are needed in total?

In the morning a warehouse split its 176 sacks of flour equally between 2 vans. The driver of the first van delivered 70 sacks before lunch. In the early afternoon a bakery returned 45 surplus sacks, which went back into that same van. Each sack still in the van holds 9 kilograms of flour. During the evening 217 kilograms from the van were used at the night bakery. How many kilograms of flour remain in the first van?

A drama club printed 207 programmes for its show. It threw away 24 that had come out of the printer smudged. Every remaining programme was sold at 3 pounds each on the night. The printing bill of 200 pounds was paid out of those takings. A patron then added 65 pounds to the same fund, and the costume hire took 308 pounds back out of it. The club has been putting on this show for a dozen seasons. How many pounds does the club have left?

A tiling firm had 237 boxes of slate in its yard and bought 8 more from a shop that was closing. Every box holds 4 tiles. A driver added 7 loose tiles that had been rattling about in his van. The whole stock was then shared equally between 3 building sites. Each tile delivered to the first site weighs 7 kilograms, and 33 kilograms of broken pieces were later swept up and carted away from that site. The firm bills its labour in minutes rather than hours. How many kilograms of slate does the first site have left?

An orchard co-op started with 17 crates and lost 8 of them to rot damage. A neighbour lent it 17 crates, and the co-op bought 47 more at auction. Every crate it now owns was filled with 9 apples from the early harvest. Sorting then removed 93 apples that were badly bruised. The rest were packed equally onto 4 lorries, and the first lorry left at dawn. The orchard covers 38 hectares, and the co-op has been trading for a dozen years. How many apples were on the first lorry?

A print works produced 206 posters on each of 3 days. Of those, 500 were posted out to shops around the county. Every poster still at the works was folded into 4 panels for the leaflet racks. Each panel carries printing on 2 sides. The works has 15 staff on the day shift. How many printed sides are there on the folded posters?

Early in the morning a market gardener cut 81 bunches of stocks. Each bunch was tied from 9 stems. Every stem carried 3 open flowers when it was cut. In the afternoon a helper brought in 48 more flowers from the polytunnel. Just before closing that evening a customer returned 23 flowers that had not fitted in her vase. How many flowers does the gardener have altogether?

A scout hut counted 35 board games in its cupboard. A jumble sale brought in another 35, and a family donated 23 more. A playgroup that was closing passed on a further 51 games. The whole collection was then shared equally between 4 huts in the district, with the Riverbank hut receiving the first share. The cupboard door has been broken for a dozen weeks. How many games went to the Riverbank hut?

Nadia baked 19 scones on Sunday morning. She dropped 2 of them on the kitchen floor and had to bin them. Her brother Sam, who had baked far fewer than Nadia that weekend, ate 10 straight off the rack. She gave 2 more to the postman at the door. Another 3 went to the neighbours across the road, and Nadia writes her baking times in minutes rather than hours. How many scones does Nadia have left?

A farm shop opened the morning with 73 punnets of strawberries. A grower's van added 41 more punnets before the doors opened. Every punnet on the shelf holds 6 strawberries. A picker dropped off 10 loose strawberries at midday for the tasting bowl. Through the afternoon and evening customers bought 455 strawberries in all. The shop has sold this variety for a dozen summers. How many strawberries are left in the shop?

A soup kitchen began the morning with 18 sacks of lentils and took delivery of 79 more. Every sack holds 9 kilograms. A grocer added 20 kilograms of loose lentils at midday, and a school harvest festival sent over 65 kilograms more. Through the afternoon the kitchen cooked with 664 kilograms of what it had. In the evening a wholesaler dropped off another 68 kilograms. The kitchen serves its meals at 12 long tables. How many kilograms of lentils does the kitchen hold now?

A cycling club sold 161 tickets for its annual dinner in the first week. Another 57 went in the second week, and a further 75 were taken at the clubhouse door. Every ticket was priced at 5 pounds. The caterer's bill of 372 pounds came straight out of the ticket money. A member then handed in 37 pounds she had collected in a jar, and the club has run this dinner for a dozen years. How many pounds does the club have from the dinner?

A pottery had 30 glazed jugs on its shelf and sent 18 of them to a gallery. Over the next month the number of jugs left on that shelf doubled. The potter then split the shelf's jugs equally between 3 market stalls. At the first stall 6 jugs were broken when a table collapsed. A new firing sent 41 jugs to that same stall, and by Sunday 37 of the stall's jugs had been sold. The kiln reaches 1200 degrees. How many jugs does the first stall have left?

Ines began her collection with 54 postcards in a shoebox. Her friend Luca, who owns fewer than she does, gave her 22 from his own box. She then posted 54 of hers to family abroad. A market stall sold her 80 postcards in a single lot, and a cousin sent 15 more in an envelope. Her grandmother added 3 very old ones from the attic. Ines has been collecting for a dozen years. How many postcards does Ines have now?

Early on Saturday morning Amira had 204 pots on her nursery bench, and she sold 85 of them straight away. Every pot still on the bench holds 5 seedlings. Her assistant Bruno, who had grown far fewer than Amira, added 26 loose seedlings from his own tray. During the afternoon a landscaper took 128 seedlings for a hedge planting. In the evening a school collected 157 more seedlings for its garden club. Amira has run this nursery for a dozen years. How many seedlings are left on the bench?

A community trust owns 230 chairs and shares them equally between its 5 halls. The warden of the Elm hall, Mr. Chen, hired out every chair in his hall at 7 pounds each for a wedding. His colleague Ms. Rowe, whose hall took far less money that weekend, keeps her accounts separately. Repairs to the Elm hall floor cost 281 pounds out of that hire money, and a cleaning bill took another 32 pounds. The trust's minibus carries 17 passengers, and the halls are booked in minutes rather than hours. How many pounds does Mr. Chen have left from the hire?

Priya rode 101 kilometres on each of 3 days at the start of her charity tour. On the fourth day she covered another 75 kilometres, and on the fifth she managed 78. A short evening loop added 5 kilometres to her total. Her friend Devan, who rode fewer kilometres than Priya on every single day, joined her for the final 25 kilometres, which she also added to her own tally. Priya's cycle computer reports distances in metres, though she writes them up in kilometres. How many kilometres has Priya ridden in total?

On Monday morning a bookshop split 24 boxes equally between its 4 delivery vans. The driver of the first van, Tomas, then loaded 70 more boxes that had been waiting on the pavement. Every box in his van holds 9 books. During the afternoon Tomas delivered 265 books to schools around the county, while his colleague Ruth delivered far fewer from her own van. The bookshop's window display holds 48 titles. How many books are still in Tomas's van?

In the morning a depot split its 212 boxes equally between 2 stores. Before lunch 36 boxes from the first store were sold across the counter. In the early afternoon a supplier delivered 20 more boxes to that same store. Every box in the first store holds 6 tins. In the evening a customer returned 49 loose tins, which were shelved with the rest. How many tins does the first store have now?
